title: Qwen3-TTS NPU graphs: batch prefill while preserving request state
summary: Amortize host dispatch with captured prefill/decode and codec graphs, bounded admission and reusable request slots.

hardware: Ascend 910B1 source campaign; other devices require independent qualification
software: InferMatrixLab/qwen3-tts-engine source snapshot; consult source evidence for measured revisions
conditions: Ascend graph support and prepared buffers for supported shapes.
Decode capacity, prefill admission and codec batching must be tuned under the actual workload.

claims.description: The runtime combines iteration-level scheduling, slot-owned KV, batched prefill and graph-captured codec state.
Prefill bucket padding appends dummy rows whose outputs are not admitted as real requests; attention masks and real lengths remain part of the computation.

downstream_impact: vLLM-Omni: reuse its scheduler, request identities and graph ownership; copying the standalone arena is not a drop-in optimization.
Graph capture and batch policy are separate hypotheses. Measure first-audio latency as well as throughput before choosing admission sizes.
recommendations: Treat each mechanism as a separate transfer experiment; do not multiply isolated or combined-stack gains.
validation_plan: Exercise changing batch sizes, mixed prompt lengths, graph misses, cancellation, slot reuse and capacity growth.
Verify retained outputs are not overwritten by subsequent replays and dummy rows cannot become requests.
Separate startup capture and warmup from timed service; repeat paired baseline/candidate workloads with lifecycle and quality checks.
limitations: Unseen shapes can incur capture work during service.
Larger admission batches may improve throughput while delaying first audio.
Standalone combined-stack measurements do not isolate graph or scheduler contributions.
Imported source guidance only; no InferRSI accelerator, audio-quality or end-to-end reproduction.
